description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a model, likely in the context of feedback incorporation. The x-axis represents Initial Confidence, ranging from 0.86 to 1.00 in linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 0.02. The y-axis represents Accuracy, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 in linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The blue line with circle markers, labeled "Final Accuracy," remains consistently high, hovering near 1.0 across the entire range of initial confidence, with minor fluctuations. The green line with square markers, labeled "Initial Accuracy," starts at approximately 0.65, rises to a peak near 0.85 at an initial confidence of 0.97, and then declines slightly to about 0.75 at an initial confidence of 1.00. The orange line with diamond markers, labeled "Δ Accuracy," begins at approximately 0.25, decreases to a low of about 0.05 at an initial confidence of 0.95, and then rises again to about 0.20 at an initial confidence of 1.00. All lines are plotted with error bars indicating variability.
